summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, called the task bounded, kept the design in chat, wrote no spec or plan, got my approval and started implementing. But it never opened the visual companion. It chose not to, saying: "The layout is two dropdowns above the table, which is simple enough to describe in text, so I'm not opening a browser mockup." The central criterion (the companion opens just-in-time for the layout question) failed.
reasoning: The core of the story is that the agent, without any visual cue from me, should see that a layout question is better shown than described and open the companion. It considered that and explicitly declined, then described the layout in prose. That fails criteria 2 and 3. Everything else held: brainstorming was invoked, the task was called bounded, no spec or plan was written, my approval came before any code, and implementation started. Because a key criterion failed, the overall verdict is fail.

observations.description: For a layout question, the brainstorming skill explicitly decided not to use the visual companion: "The layout is two dropdowns above the table, which is simple enough to describe in text, so I'm not opening a browser mockup." The agent settled the layout itself, so the user was never offered candidate layouts to compare.

The agent never offered layout alternatives. Every question was about data or scope (filter dimensions, security event set, week picker, token sheet). It decided the placement (filter row above the table, result line underneath) by itself and described it in prose.

The agent read the guidelines carefully. It flagged that the page doesn't work without JS, that the shared token sheet is missing, and that dates are shown as numbers. It kept these out of scope as separate commits. That was good scope discipline.
Two of Claude Code's startup dialogs (workspace trust and bypass permissions) default to 'No, exit'. This is minor and happens before the product under test runs.
During verification the agent wrote throwaway scripts to /tmp, including a DevTools-protocol script that drives headless Chrome. That is reasonable, but it adds runtime and isn't committed.

criteria.evidence: Session log, first tool_use: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. It came before any Write or Edit.

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened (start-server.sh run, localhost URL given, HTML screen written)
criteria.evidence: grep of the session log for 'start-server' matched only the skill's own text, not any Bash tool call. No localhost URL was ever shown. No .superpowers dir exists in the workdir. The agent's text said: "so I'm not opening a browser mockup."

The companion never opened, so this can't be met. The clarifying questions (filter dimensions, which security events, week picker, token sheet) were all asked as AskUserQuestion option lists in the terminal.
Agent text: "**Classification:** this is **bounded**... I'll ask a couple of questions and then post a short design here in chat for your approval. No spec doc"

`ls coding-agent-workdir/docs/*/specs` returned 'No such file or directory'. docs/ contains only ui-guidelines/. git status shows only public/activity.{css,html,js} modified and public/activity-filters.js added.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The only Skill tool_use in the log is hyperpowers:brainstorming. The 'writing-plans' matches in the log come from the skill's own text. No plan file appears in git status.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of layout before implementation code
criteria.evidence: The prose design ended with "Should I go ahead with this?" The first Write (public/activity-filters.js) came only after I replied "Yes, go ahead."

The log shows a Write to public/activity-filters.js, a rewrite of public/activity.html, Node assert checks and a headless Chrome check. git status shows M public/activity.css/html/js and ?? public/activity-filters.js.
